personality_voice.book_baseline: Across all seven books, Hagrid's personality is one of the most consistent and distinctively rendered in the series. His core traits are: warm, emotionally transparent, fiercely loyal, enthusiastically naive about dangerous creatures, prone to accidental disclosure when emotionally engaged or flattered, physically imposing but gentle, and possessed of an immediately recognizable dialect (dropped consonants, non-standard grammar, short emphatic sentences). Secondary traits include wounded pride when underestimated, comic domestic warmth, rueful self-awareness about his own limitations, capacity for public emotional outbursts, and an inability to lie convincingly under pressure. The most book-important installments for personality establishment are PS (foundational), CoS (domestic warmth, rule-bending complexity), PoA (emotional depth, Azkaban trauma), and GoF (vulnerability, shame spiral). OotP, HBP, and DH add behavioral texture without fundamentally changing the established type.
personality_voice.film_portrayal: The films preserve Hagrid's dialect with high consistency across all installments — the phonetic speech pattern is one of the most faithfully reproduced elements in the entire adaptation. His warmth, creature enthusiasm, and protectiveness are present in every film. Key personality moments are well-rendered: the accidental disclosure pattern (PS, repeatedly), the emotional openness (crying at multiple points across films), the fierce defense of Dumbledore, the domestic comedy (rock cakes, treacle fudge in CoS), and the physical warmth. The DH Burrow rambling speech is one of the most faithful single characterization moments in the corpus. His creature enthusiasm is consistently present. His moral directness about friendship (PoA reconciliation scene, CoS defense of Hermione) is preserved.
personality_voice.difference: The aggregated losses across all books are: (1) The GoF shame spiral and interior voice — his weeks of hiding, self-deprecating humor about his own failures, the heritage confession to Maxime — are entirely absent, removing his most emotionally complex book-level personality expression. (2) The PoA Azkaban trauma confession and the drunk scene, which show him as both brave and scarred, are absent. (3) The OotP sustained behavioral texture — prolonged deflections, stubbornness under Umbridge, the pub scene's oblique emotional intelligence — is compressed to brief exchanges. (4) The HBP sulking/reconciliation arc and Snape intelligence leak, which showed wounded pride and compulsive disclosure respectively, are absent. (5) The PS hospital wing self-condemnation scene, the fullest explicit expression of his disclosure guilt, is absent. Cumulatively, the films preserve the surface personality (dialect, warmth, loyalty, creature enthusiasm) but remove most of the behavioral material that made him contradictory, surprising, and psychologically layered across the series.
personality_voice.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across all per-book scorings with specific scene-level citations.
personality_voice.penalty_logic: The surface personality is among the most faithfully adapted of any major HP character — the dialect performance and warmth are genuinely strong. However, the cumulative loss of interior complexity across six of the seven books is substantial. No single book's personality losses are catastrophic, but together they consistently strip the same secondary layer: emotional vulnerability, self-aware complexity, behavioral contradiction. The film Hagrid is always recognizable but is systematically simplified toward the 'lovable gentle giant' archetype and away from the specific, scarred, contradictory, naively compulsive figure the books construct. Per-book personality scores ranged from 17 (GoF, worst) to 22 (PS, best), with most clustering at 18–21. The synthesis reflects a strong preservation of surface traits penalized by consistent secondary losses. Score: 20.

narrative_role_agency.book_baseline: Hagrid's narrative role across the series is unusually multi-functional for a supporting character. He is the initiating agent of Harry's entry into the wizarding world (PS); the plot-driving information source whose disclosures move multiple climaxes (PS flute/Fluffy/Flamel, GoF dragon reveal, PoA Three Broomsticks); the executor of Dumbledore's highest-stakes missions (PS Gringotts, OotP giants, DH Seven Potters); an active combatant (OotP forced removal, DH aerial chase and motorbike self-sacrifice, DH Battle of Hogwarts); a subplot anchor whose presence or absence creates narrative stakes (CoS arrest, OotP absence/return); and a moral and emotional agent who confronts, reconciles, and shapes character relationships. His most important single agentic moments across the series are: PS flute gift enabling the Fluffy passage, GoF dragon reveal, PoA Three Broomsticks testimony, OotP Astronomy Tower resistance, DH motorbike self-sacrifice.
narrative_role_agency.film_portrayal: The films preserve Hagrid's role as Harry's initiating guide (PS), his accidental disclosure function (PS Fluffy/Flamel, functional if the flute mechanism is transferred), the GoF dragon reveal as his own initiative, the CoS 'follow the spiders' clue, the DH Seven Potters transportation role, his role carrying Harry's body in DH, and his participation in the Battle of Hogwarts. His emotional anchor function is consistently present. His Gringotts mission (PS) and giant mission (OotP) are preserved in reduced/expository form.
narrative_role_agency.difference: Aggregated agency losses across the series: (1) PS: the flute's practical climactic function transferred to Snape's harp — the causal chain survives informationally but the physical gift loses its plot consequence. (2) PoA: Three Broomsticks testimony transferred entirely to McGonagall/Fudge — Hagrid's most significant act of narrative participation in that installment's backstory exposition. (3) GoF: teaching role, Karkaroff confrontation, weeks-long absence subplot, and secret Dumbledore mission all absent — he becomes primarily the dragon-reveal agent rather than a multi-function active character. (4) OotP: Astronomy Tower resistance scene entirely absent — his most agentive, physically dramatic moment in the book is not dramatized; giant mission compressed from active multi-stage operation to exposition. (5) HBP: staff meeting participation, funeral procession, Diagon Alley escort, and Snape intelligence leak all absent. (6) DH: motorbike self-sacrifice (throwing himself at a Death Eater) absent — his most dramatic single act of heroism in the corpus is removed. Across six of seven books, meaningful agency is either transferred or simply removed.
narrative_role_agency.evidence_status: Directly evidenced. Transfer Rule applied to PS flute mechanism and PoA Three Broomsticks testimony. Removals without transfer documented for OotP Astronomy Tower, DH motorbike sacrifice, HBP staff meeting, GoF Karkaroff confrontation.
narrative_role_agency.penalty_logic: The per-book agency scores ranged from 13 (OotP, HBP, GoF) to 17 (PS). The consistent pattern is that the films preserve Hagrid's single most important plot-critical act per book while removing most surrounding agency. He never becomes decorative — there is always at least one meaningful act per film — but his role is systematically reduced from multi-function active agent to single-function warm presence. The two most significant series-level agency losses are: the OotP Astronomy Tower removal (shows his genuine power and unconquerable resistance) and the DH motorbike self-sacrifice (his greatest physical heroism in the corpus). Both are absent. The PoA Three Broomsticks transfer is the clearest Transfer Rule violation. The cumulative effect is a character whose narrative function is consistently thinner than the books establish. Score: 14.

motivations_internal_conflict.book_baseline: Hagrid's motivations across the series are consistent at the core — loyalty to Dumbledore, love for Harry, passion for creatures, desire to be trusted and worthy — but each book adds a specific layer of internal conflict or motivational texture: PS (guilt over accidental disclosure vs. duty to secrecy; need to prove himself trustworthy after expulsion); CoS (creature love overriding practical caution, fear of Azkaban); PoA (love of Buckbeak vs. Azkaban fear creating tragic paralysis; desire to succeed as teacher); GoF (half-giant shame and the internal conflict between hiding and accepting his heritage, crystallized in the Skeeter crisis); OotP (loyalty vs. survival, love of family creating irrational risk with Grawp, fear of sacking vs. refusal to compromise); HBP (wounded pride vs. affection for the trio; knowledge of dangerous information vs. impulse to share); DH (protective love vs. terror, self-reproach for practical failures alongside heroic resolve).
motivations_internal_conflict.film_portrayal: The core motivations are preserved across all films: loyalty to Dumbledore, love for Harry, creature enthusiasm, protectiveness. The specific internal conflicts are variably handled. CoS fear of Azkaban is present. PoA Buckbeak grief is present but the Azkaban fear-paralysis is absent. GoF heritage shame and collapse are entirely absent. OotP Grawp motivation is present at surface level ('he's my brother') but the deeper identification with abandonment is absent. HBP wounded pride arc is absent. DH self-reproach for the sidecar damage is absent. The disclosure guilt (PS) is shown in self-correction but the full hospital wing reckoning is absent.
motivations_internal_conflict.difference: The most significant motivational losses across the series are: GoF — the entire half-giant shame internal conflict, the defining motivation of that installment, is absent; PoA — the Azkaban fear-paralysis, which makes his passivity tragic rather than merely sad, is absent; OotP — the pub scene identification with Harry as fellow orphan/outsider, the emotional engine of his Grawp motivation, is absent; PS — the hospital wing guilt, the fullest explicit articulation of his disclosure conflict, is absent. The pattern is consistent: surface motivations (love, loyalty, creature passion) are preserved; deeper motivational conflicts (shame, fear, guilt, identification) are removed.
motivations_internal_conflict.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across per-book scorings. The GoF heritage shame absence is the most significant single motivational loss in the series.
motivations_internal_conflict.penalty_logic: Per-book motivation scores ranged from 10 (GoF, worst) to 13 (PS, PoA, DH). The GoF collapse is the clearest case of a core book-specific motivation being entirely absent from the film. Across the series, the films consistently preserve the simple motivational substrate while stripping the specific internal conflict that gives each book's Hagrid his particular texture. The result is a Hagrid who is always understandable but never as conflicted or as psychologically rich as the books establish. Score: 12.

character_arc.book_baseline: Hagrid's arc across the series has two levels. At the macro level, he moves from trusted gamekeeper/outsider figure to fully integrated member of the Order and teacher, tested by increasing danger, loss, and moral complexity, but unwavering in loyalty — culminating in carrying Harry's apparent corpse and surviving the final battle. At the book level, each installment has a distinct arc: PS (flaw manifested → guilt → forgiveness); CoS (presence → arrest/absence → restoration); PoA (pride → crisis → grief → relief); GoF (pride → exposure/shame/collapse → recovery → renewed commitment — the most complete personal arc in the series); OotP (return under threat → deterioration → defiance/departure → partial comfort attempt); HBP (hopeful start → Aragog grief → institutional anxiety → Dumbledore grief → commitment to stay); DH (protector under fire → endurance → grief → survival). GoF is the most important arc book; OotP and PoA also have substantial arc content.
character_arc.film_portrayal: The films preserve Hagrid's macro arc as a series-level emotional throughline — he is consistently present, consistently loyal, and his survival and reunion with Harry in DH provide a satisfying series-level resolution. At the book level: PS arc is compressed (nadir absent); CoS arc is structurally preserved; PoA arc is present in broad shape but steps are skipped; GoF arc is essentially absent (collapse and recovery are the arc, and they are cut); OotP arc is incomplete (deterioration phase absent, climactic removal absent, final comfort beat absent); HBP arc is compressed (institutional dimension and resolution commitment absent); DH arc is appropriately flat and preserved.
character_arc.difference: The GoF arc is the most significant single arc failure in the series: the collapse-and-recovery is the entire arc, and the film presents a flat Hagrid who begins and ends at approximately the same emotional register. This is not compression but absence. The OotP arc is the second-most significant failure: the Astronomy Tower removal — the arc's climax — is not dramatized, and the final comfort attempt is cut, leaving the arc without a climax or resolution. The PoA arc is compressed but structurally intact. The PS and CoS arcs are largely preserved. The HBP and DH arcs are appropriately compact and reasonably preserved.
character_arc.evidence_status: Directly evidenced. GoF arc failure is the clearest series-level arc problem.
character_arc.penalty_logic: Per-book arc scores ranged from 10 (GoF, OotP) to 13 (PS, CoS, DH). The GoF and OotP failures are the most damaging because those are two of the three books where Hagrid has the most substantial personal arc. The synthesis must weight GoF heavily as the book in which Hagrid's arc is most fully developed and most completely lost. The macro series arc is preserved but the two most important book-level arcs are significantly compromised. Score: 11.

key_relationships.book_baseline: Hagrid's key relationships across the series are: (1) Harry — the defining relationship, established in PS and developed through all books; characterised by paternal protectiveness, mutual identification (both outsiders), and reciprocal care; most richly expressed in GoF (mutual identification, Harry's protective lying) and OotP (pub scene, shared orphan/outsider status). (2) Dumbledore — absolute loyalty, near-reverence, reciprocally confirmed trust; most explicitly dramatised in PS and HBP. (3) Harry/Ron/Hermione trio collectively — warm, domestic, mutual; most textured in CoS, PoA, and HBP. (4) Madame Maxime — romantic longing built on shared identity; the defining secondary relationship of GoF, showing his vulnerability and longing for belonging. (5) Aragog — recurring creature-love relationship, most important in CoS and HBP. (6) Antagonistic/institutional relationships: Umbridge (OotP), Lucius Malfoy (CoS), Karkaroff (GoF), Filch (HBP).
key_relationships.film_portrayal: The Harry-Hagrid relationship is preserved in its emotional core across all films — the founding bond, the physical protectiveness, the grief and reunion beats. The Dumbledore relationship is emotionally present (loyalty, devastation at his death). The trio relationship is present but consistently thinner than the books. The Aragog relationship is well-rendered in CoS and HBP. Umbridge dynamic is present in abbreviated form. Karkaroff confrontation is absent. Maxime relationship is present in GoF as romantic courtship but loses its defining dramatic function (the heritage recognition, the shattering rejection, the revelation scene).
key_relationships.difference: The most significant series-level relational losses are: (1) GoF Maxime relationship — the revelation scene (Hagrid's vulnerability, longing for belonging, Maxime's denial and departure) is cut, removing the fullest dramatization of Hagrid's emotional vulnerability and longing for shared identity in the entire series. (2) OotP pub scene — the Harry-Hagrid mutual identification as orphans and outsiders, the emotional engine of their relationship in that book, is absent. (3) Harry-comforts-Hagrid reciprocity (PS hospital wing, various PoA and GoF moments) — the relational dynamic is consistently presented as Hagrid giving care rather than receiving it, flattening the reciprocal dimension. (4) HBP trio estrangement/reconciliation — the most complex relational moment between Hagrid and the trio in that book is absent. (5) Karkaroff confrontation absent in GoF — his fierce loyalty expressed through physical aggression is not shown.
key_relationships.evidence_status: Directly evidenced. The Maxime revelation scene absence is the single largest relational loss in the series.
key_relationships.penalty_logic: Per-book relationship scores ranged from 6 (GoF, worst) to 8 (PS, CoS, PoA). The consistent pattern is that emotional cores are preserved while relational texture and depth are lost. The two most significant losses are the Maxime revelation scene (the deepest expression of Hagrid's vulnerability in the series) and the OotP pub scene (the deepest expression of the Harry-Hagrid mutual identification). Both are entirely absent. Score: 7.

complexity_nuance_lost_material.book_baseline: Hagrid's complexity across the series rests on a set of recurring contradictions: (1) trusted by Dumbledore with high-stakes missions yet constitutionally incapable of keeping secrets; (2) physically powerful but emotionally fragile and easily shamed; (3) knowledgeable and tactically capable in his domain yet recklessly naive about danger to others; (4) brave under fire yet paralyzed by specific fears (Azkaban); (5) emotionally generous and warm yet capable of sulking, wounded pride, and self-imposed isolation; (6) able to show situational intelligence (the coded farewell in CoS, the pub scene emotional intelligence in OotP) while being utterly guileless in other contexts (the Rita Skeeter interview in GoF); (7) a man whose greatest flaw (unconditional creature love, compulsive disclosure) and greatest strength (unconditional loyalty, fearless protectiveness) are aspects of the same underlying trait. The books that contribute most to this complexity are GoF (shame, heritage, collapse), OotP (sustained deterioration, pub scene, Astronomy Tower resistance), PoA (Azkaban trauma, drunk scene), and PS (hospital wing guilt, expulsion wound).
complexity_nuance_lost_material.film_portrayal: The films consistently preserve the broad strokes: the warmth, the dialect, the creature love, the loyalty, the physical comedy, the grief. Several specific complexity beats are well-executed: the DH Burrow rambling speech (awareness of his own suspicious appearance, comic vulnerability), the CoS 'follow the spiders' coded farewell (situational intelligence), the PoA reconciliation engineering (caring for others while suffering), the HBP Aragog grief (the tragedy of loving what nearly killed his friends). The GoF campfire warmth and the OotP Grawp motivation are present at surface level.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.difference: Cumulatively, the films remove almost all of the material that makes Hagrid contradictory rather than simply lovable. Absent: GoF shame spiral and heritage conflict (his deepest vulnerability); PoA Azkaban fear-paralysis (brave yet terrified); PoA drunk scene (self-flagellating guilt, protectiveness-via-anger); PS hospital wing guilt (full self-reckoning); OotP pub scene (emotional intelligence about shared dispossession); OotP Astronomy Tower resistance (unconquerable refusal to be subdued); OotP Thestral inspection humiliation (dignity under systematic attack); DH motorbike self-sacrifice (greatest physical heroism in corpus); GoF Maxime revelation (deepest vulnerability, longing for belonging); HBP sulking/reconciliation arc (wounded pride); HBP Snape intelligence leak (compulsive disclosure even under pressure). The pattern is consistent across seven books: the films retain the warmth while removing the contradictions. The result is a Hagrid who is a beloved archetype — the loyal, lovable gentle giant — rather than the specific, scarred, contradictory figure the books construct.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.evidence_status: Directly evidenced across all per-book scorings. The pattern of consistent selective removal is itself evidenced by the uniformity of the losses across installments.
complexity_nuance_lost_material.penalty_logic: Per-book complexity scores ranged from 8 (GoF, OotP) to 11 (PS). No book achieves the top range. The losses are not concentrated in one installment but are distributed across the series, suggesting a systematic rather than incidental pattern of simplification. The most damaging losses for complexity are GoF (the shame spiral is his most psychologically rich arc in the series), PoA (the Azkaban confession is his most psychologically dense single scene), and OotP (the Astronomy Tower removal is his most agentive and defiant single act). Together these three books provide most of the material that distinguishes book-Hagrid from the archetype the films largely present. Score: 9.

comparative.key_observations: Rubeus Hagrid is one of the more recognizable major-character adaptations in the Harry Potter films — the dialect performance is consistent and strong, the warmth and loyalty are present in every installment, and the films reliably preserve his single most plot-critical act per book. However, the synthesis reveals a systematic pattern of simplification across the entire series: the films consistently retain Hagrid's surface archetype (loyal, warm, creature-obsessed, emotionally open) while removing the specific material that made him contradictory, psychologically rich, and agentively significant. The five most damaging losses at the series level are: (1) the GoF shame spiral and collapse — his most complete personal arc in the series, entirely absent; (2) the OotP Astronomy Tower resistance — his most agentive and defiant single moment, not dramatized; (3) the PoA Azkaban fear-paralysis — his most psychologically dense single scene, absent; (4) the DH motorbike self-sacrifice — his greatest physical heroism in the corpus, removed; and (5) the GoF Maxime revelation — the deepest expression of his vulnerability in the series, cut. The result is a film Hagrid who is genuinely beloved and substantially recognizable but who has been systematically reduced from a specific, scarred, contradictory figure — brave yet terrified, trusted yet constitutionally incapable of keeping secrets, emotionally generous yet capable of wounded pride and shame collapse — to a simpler, warmer, more passive version. The final score of 73 reflects strong surface fidelity penalized by consistent, book-spanning losses in agency, internal conflict, arc depth, and the complexity that distinguishes the character from his own archetype.
